history: Initially discovered in the United States ~70 years ago. Most widely spread sweet potato virus worldwide, recently identified in Italy as primary contributor to SPVD.

proteins.name: HC-Pro
proteins.function: Proteinase, aids in aphid transmission, long-distance movement

proteins.name: CI
proteins.function: Cytoplasmic inclusion protein, RNA helicase activity

proteins.name: Cistron
proteins.function: Coat protein, virion assembly, viral transmission, spread

life_cycle.entry: Mechanical or vector-mediated via aphid stylets
life_cycle.replication: Genome translated into polyprotein, cleaved by P1, HC-Pro, NIa proteases

host_range: Ipomoea spp. (I. alba, I. aquatica, I. heredifolia, I. nil, I. lacunosa, I. purpurea, I. cordatotriloba, I. tricolor)
Nicotiana spp. (N. benthamiana, N. rustica, N. tabacum)

co-infections.SPVD: Occurs when SPFMV co-infects with SPCSV; causes stunted growth, severe mosaic, leaf distortion, reduced yield
co-infections.synergism_effects: SPFMV titers up to 600x higher in SPVD; enhanced spread and replication

strains.name: C
strains.location: Australia, Africa, Asia, North and South America

genetic_variability.mutation_sources: Geographical separation; coat protein gene variation affects immune response

agricultural_impact.yield_loss: Can range from 50% to near complete loss, especially in SPVD co-infections
agricultural_impact.affected_regions: Oceania, Southern Africa, Barbados, other SPVD-affected areas
agricultural_impact.social_impact: Impacts subsistence farmers relying on sweet potato as staple food

management.removal: Remove infected plants to prevent spread
prevention: Properly clean tools to prevent mechanical transmission
Use transgenic plants expressing antiviral genes

references: Various sources from plant virology and sweet potato disease studies as cited in user-provided content
